evals.prompt: Our API's memory keeps climbing over a day and we restart it every night. Can you audit evals/files/sample-repo for memory and resource leaks and give us a procedure to prove whether the fix works?
evals.expected_output: Findings with the LEAK prefix for: the undisposed FileStream in ReportService.Export, the static List in RequestAudit that only grows, the unbounded user-keyed IMemoryCache in ProductCache.Remember (with AddMemoryCache() lacking SizeLimit), and the StockSyncWorker empty catch plus growing _processed list. No findings for ReadTemplateAsync, SubmitAsync, _routeNames or GetOrLoad. A report containing the 15-minute load-test procedure with working set, gen2, handle count metrics and pass/fail thresholds, and the dotnet-counters commands.
expectations: Detects the stack as dotnet and loads only references/dotnet.md
Runs ../audit-code-scan/scripts/grep_scan.py with scripts/patterns/dotnet.json and records hits under audit/evidence/audit-backend-resource-leak/
Emits a finding for ReportService.Export FileStream without using, referencing CWE-772
Emits a finding for the static _requests list in RequestAudit rated Critical or High, referencing CWE-401 or CWE-770
Emits a finding for ProductCache.Remember / AddMemoryCache() without SizeLimit or expiration
Emits a finding for StockSyncWorker's empty catch block (CWE-390) and mentions the growing _processed list
Does not emit findings for ReadTemplateAsync, SubmitAsync, _routeNames, or GetOrLoad
Report contains a 15-minute load-test procedure with working set, gen2, and handle count metrics and explicit pass/fail thresholds
Report lists dotnet-counters (or dotnet-gcdump) commands
Report includes a Not checked section
All finding ids start with LEAK-
findings.json validates with ../audit-finding-writer/scripts/findings.py validate

evals.prompt: We ran the leak load test and got evals/files/samples-leaking.csv (15 s samples, 2 min warm-up). Does it pass? What should we do next?
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/leak_loadtest.py grade on the CSV, reports FAIL with the working-set slope in MB/min, notes handles rising, and recommends a heap diff (dotnet-gcdump / MAT / DevTools) to find the holder of the growing type.
expectations: Uses scripts/leak_loadtest.py grade with --baseline-minutes
Reports an overall FAIL verdict
States the working set slope in MB/min and that it exceeds the 5 MB/min fail threshold
Notes that handle count grew by more than 10%
Recommends a before/after heap diff as the next step

evals.prompt: Check the background worker in evals/files/sample-repo/Inventory.Api/Workers/StockSyncWorker.cs - is it stable for production?
evals.expected_output: One or two findings: empty catch block swallowing all exceptions in the worker loop (High), and the _processed list growing without bound across iterations. Remediation shows scope-per-iteration (already present), logging in the catch, OperationCanceledException handling, and dropping or bounding _processed.
expectations: Flags the empty catch (Exception) block with CWE-390
Flags _processed as unbounded growth
Remediation includes logging the exception with ILogger and rethrowing/exiting on OperationCanceledException when cancellation was requested
Acknowledges that the scope-per-iteration pattern is correct

evals.prompt: Second run of the leak test after we fixed the cache: samples are in evals/files/samples-flat.csv (15 s samples, 2 min warm-up). Can we call the memory stable now?
evals.expected_output: leak_loadtest.py grade is run on the CSV; working-set slope after the baseline is under 2 MB/min, last-5-min mean is within 10% of the first-5-min mean, gen2 collections stay at a steady low rate, handle and thread counts are flat. Overall PASS, with the caveat that a 15-minute run at one load level proves stability only for that load.
expectations: The grade subcommand of leak_loadtest.py is run on the CSV
Overall verdict reported is PASS
No metric row is reported as FAIL
The reply notes the result covers only the tested load level and duration
